# HELMET

> HELMET is the Wayne State app stack's baseline runtime: security headers and CSP, session hardening, trusted proxies, a /up health check, structured logs and version warnings, in one small PHP core.

GIF via [Tenor](https://tenor.com/view/helmet-band-wilmas-rainbow-helmet-band-music-gif-25658120)

**Put it on before you ship.** Security headers, a hardened session and an honest proxy check, snapped on before
the first page is served.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).
Two mirrors, one command: the only thing in this repo that plays both sides is the CI.
Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), the playbook, as static files ([`site/README.md`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/site/README.md)).
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

HELMET is the Wayne State app stack's baseline runtime. One small
framework-free PHP core, `Waynestate\Helmet`, does the five things every app on
Citadel needs before it serves a single page: it sends the security headers,
hardens the session, decides whether the request really arrived over HTTPS,
answers the load balancer's `/up` ping, and writes structured logs.

This repository is published from Wayne State University's internal
GitLab and mirrored here. Changes land there first; Wayne State
developers open issues and merge requests on the internal project.

It is the floor, not the ceiling. An app on raw PHP calls `helmet_boot()` once
at the top of its front controller and is done. An app on Laravel or a PSR-15
stack mounts the same core as middleware and gets the identical headers. The
rules live in one place, and every consumer path agrees.

Every page below is Markdown. The HTML pages send the same Markdown to a client that asks for `text/markdown`. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit from the README and the pages; do not edit.

## Pages

- [HELMET: Put it on before you ship.](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md): HELMET is the Wayne State app stack's baseline runtime: security headers and CSP, session hardening, trusted proxies, a /up health check, structured logs and version warnings, in one small PHP core.

## Prompts

- [Get started with HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-get-started): Which formation the app is in, which platform sits in front of it, and the smallest plan to put the helmet on before the first page is served. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a raw PHP app](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php): One call at the top of the front controller, the nonce on every inline script, and a health check that still answers when there is no front controller. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a Laravel app with Blade](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-blade): The adapter discovers itself; publish the config, pick the platform, keep Laravel's own /up, and nonce the inline scripts in Blade. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-inertia): The Laravel adapter plus the coach's rules: scripts in the layout, never in Inertia's Head, one nonce from one package, no shared caching of nonced HTML. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a PSR-15 middleware pipeline](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-psr15): The same core as middleware: the health check first, then the headers, and the nonce read from the request attribute downstream. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
